question: Why are straps fastened across the chest, hips, and knees during ambulance transport?

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rely on just one method to check a patient's nutrition?

question: What is the main goal of a 'just culture' in healthcare?

options.A: Ignoring minor medication errors if no patient was physically harmed

question: What main body structures do the embryonic neural tube turn into?

question: When talking to government policy makers, what do they usually care about most?

question: How can you tell over time if a patient's diet therapy is working successfully?

question: Which method is commonly used by nurse managers to evaluate if nursing documentation standards are being met?

question: According to health standards, what does reproductive health truly cover?

options.A: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being

question: What is the purpose of food security early warning systems?

question: What happens when one system, like local transport, breaks down in a community?

question: What is the primary goal of health promotion?

question: Why do nurse managers need to understand economic appraisals?

options.D: How often community members actually visit and use the services

explanation: Utilization rate measures the extent to which the target population uses available health services. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a non-probability sampling method?

options.A: Convenience sampling
options.B: Simple random sampling
options.C: Snowball sampling
options.D: Purposive sampling

explanation: Correct! Simple random sampling belongs to the probability family because it relies on pure chance, not convenience or choice. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h4)

question: Who is expected to show leadership skills in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Only senior physicians and surgical consultants
options.B: Only the director of nursing and hospital chief executive
options.C: Administrative staff who manage patient records
options.D: Every nurse, regardless of formal administrative rank

explanation: You don't need a fancy title to be a leader! Every nurse shows leadership when coordinating bedside care or supporting teammates. [learn more](GST321_U3_T1#GST321_U3_T1_h1)

question: What does a route of transmission describe?

options.A: The path a germ takes from a source to a new host
options.B: The specific medication used to kill a virus
options.C: The time it takes for symptoms to show up
options.D: The physical strength of a bacterial cell wall

explanation: The route of transmission is simply the way an infectious agent moves from its reservoir to reach a susceptible person. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do health programs brought in from the outside often fail if the locals aren't involved?

options.A: External workers refuse to build modern hospital facilities
options.B: Foreign agencies always bring too much medical equipment
options.C: Local residents are legally forbidden from talking to outsiders
options.D: They may lack cultural fit and understanding of local needs

explanation: If a program doesn't fit the actual lifestyle and traditions of the people, it won't work. Locals must be part of the plan! [learn more](GNS225_U1_T5#GNS225_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which part of the brain acts as the master pacemaker by releasing GnRH to start the menstrual cycle?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Adrenal cortex
options.C: Anterior pituitary
options.D: Ovary

explanation: The hypothalamus sends out pulses of Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH), telling the pituitary gland to kick off the whole hormone chain reaction! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h2)

question: How should a bricklayer doing heavy manual labor in the hot Nigerian sun adjust their diet compared to a desk worker?

options.A: Decrease all food intake to prevent excessive sweating
options.B: Eliminate all carbohydrates to protect joint health
options.C: Rely exclusively on vitamin supplements instead of meals
options.D: Increase total energy and macronutrient intake to match high physical exertion

explanation: Heavy physical work burns through calories fast! They need more energy and macronutrients to keep up with the hard work. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h4)

question: Which food must be strictly avoided by a patient taking a Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitor (MAOI)?

options.A: Fresh green leafy vegetables
options.B: Plain boiled white rice
options.C: Pasteurized cow's milk
options.D: Aged cheeses and cured meats

explanation: You got it! These foods are high in tyramine, which can trigger a dangerous, life-threatening spike in blood pressure when combined with MAOIs. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h6)

question: What part of a sterile field package is always considered contaminated?

options.A: The exact center of the drape
options.B: The items placed inside the wrapper
options.C: The outer one-inch border
options.D: The bottom surface resting on the table

explanation: The outer edge touches non-sterile surfaces during opening, so the outer one-inch margin is treated as contaminated. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the main goal of a 'Just Culture' in healthcare?

options.A: To place full blame on the individual nurse who carried out the order
options.B: To balance system accountability with personal responsibility for reckless acts
options.C: To ensure that no nurse is ever punished for making a medication error
options.D: To remove all hospital policies so staff can work using personal intuition

explanation: Spot on! A Just Culture knows how to tell the difference between a simple human slip, a risky habit, and outright recklessness, treating each one fairly. [learn more](GST319_U6_T7#GST319_U6_T7_h4)

question: Which two organs are most commonly affected by hydatid cysts in the human body?

options.A: Liver and lungs
options.B: Heart and spleen
options.C: Stomach and pancreas
options.D: Brain and kidneys

explanation: The liver acts as the first major capillary filter for blood returning from the intestines, making it the most common site, with the lungs second. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T25#GNS313_U2_T25_h5)

question: What is a common mistake nurses should avoid when assessing patients during a disaster?

options.A: Spending too much time on detailed checks for one stable patient
options.B: Applying pressure bandages immediately to actively bleeding wounds
options.C: Checking vital signs and airway status before administering any drugs
options.D: Prioritizing patients tagged red before addressing walking wounded

explanation: In a mass casualty setting, spending all your time on one stable patient means others who are critical might miss out on care. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h6)

question: A patient needs an allergy drug for daytime use that won't make them sleepy on their heavy-machinery job. Which one is best?

options.A: Promethazine
options.B: Loratadine
options.C: Chlorpheniramine
options.D: Diphenhydramine

explanation: Brilliant choice! Loratadine is a second-generation antihistamine that doesn't cross easily into the brain, keeping your patient alert and safe at work. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T8#GNS215_U6_T8_h2)

question: Which group is usually formed by local neighbors to tackle specific health needs in their area?

options.A: Community-Based Organizations
options.B: International pharmaceutical firms
options.C: Global trade syndicates
options.D: Federal ministries of health

explanation: Spot on! Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) start right at the grassroots level because local people know what their neighborhood needs most. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h2)

question: A nursing student writes this objective: 'To study everything about nurses.' Which SMART rule does this break the most?

options.A: Specific
options.B: Financial
options.C: Time-bound
options.D: Ethical

explanation: Saying 'everything about nurses' is way too broad! A good objective needs to be Specific so you know exactly what corner of nursing you are investigating. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h5)

question: Why is writing up your transport documentation right after a medevac mission so important?

options.A: Receiving hospitals require it to calculate parking fees
options.B: Transport nurses need it to log their personal mileage
options.C: Insurance companies use it only to check vehicle speeds
options.D: It provides a clear legal record of care and ensures continuity

explanation: Good records protect both you and the patient. They make sure the next caregivers know the full story, and they serve as an official legal record. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h9)

question: Why is it crucial to quickly report abnormal vital signs to the doctor?

options.A: It ensures the hospital bed can be reassigned to another patient quickly
options.B: It proves the nurse completed all assigned tasks for the morning
options.C: It allows the healthcare team to intervene before the patient's condition worsens
options.D: It removes the need to monitor the patient for the rest of the day

explanation: Quick communication lets the medical team step in fast and prevent emergencies. Your quick thinking saves lives! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h9)

question: Why does the law treat young offenders differently from adult criminals?

options.A: Juveniles are completely immune to all forms of criminal prosecution
options.B: Minors possess developing brains that affect impulse control and judgment
options.C: Prisons are entirely unsuitable for holding individuals under twenty
options.D: Young offenders never commit violent crimes that harm society

explanation: Great thinking! Teen brains are still growing, which means they sometimes struggle with impulse control. The justice system recognizes this and focuses more on guidance. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT something a community health nurse should do?

options.A: Ignoring community input to enforce rapid medical compliance
options.B: Advocating for fair resource distribution among marginalized groups
options.C: Respecting cultural traditions while promoting health education
options.D: Protecting patient confidentiality during home visits

explanation: Correct! Community nursing is all about teamwork and partnership—we never force things, but rather work together with the people we care for. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T7#GNS225_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the main goal of the Model for Improvement in healthcare?

options.A: To increase the total number of administrative reports filled out daily
options.B: To replace traditional nursing judgment with computer algorithms
options.C: To help clinical teams make practical changes that improve patient outcomes
options.D: To punish staff members who make mistakes during patient care

explanation: You got this! The model is simply a guide to help healthcare workers make meaningful, tested changes that make patient care better every day. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of the pulmonary circulation system?

options.A: To deliver nutrient-rich blood directly to the brain
options.B: To pump blood against a very high vascular resistance
options.C: To filter waste products out of systemic blood vessels
options.D: To exchange carbon dioxide for oxygen in the lungs

explanation: The primary function of pulmonary circulation is to move blood through the lungs so carbon dioxide can be dropped off and fresh oxygen picked up. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: What must a participant give before answering a research questionnaire?

options.A: Proof of health insurance
options.B: A physician's referral letter
options.C: A notarized identity card
options.D: Informed consent

explanation: Participants must voluntarily agree to take part after being fully informed about the study's purpose. Ethical nursing practice starts here! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h7)

question: What is the medical term for pale, bulky, foul-smelling stools caused by unabsorbed dietary fat?

options.A: Steatorrhea
options.B: Hematuria
options.C: Proteinuria
options.D: Glycosuria

explanation: Spot on! Steatorrhea is the clinical term for fatty stools that happen when the body fails to absorb lipids properly. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T006#GNS227_U6_T006_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI)?

options.A: Reducing childhood mortality rates across the country
options.B: Protecting infants from vaccine-preventable infectious diseases
options.C: Completely eliminating all chronic genetic disorders in children
options.D: Building community immunity against dangerous pathogens

explanation: Correct! EPI focuses on infectious, vaccine-preventable diseases. Genetic disorders are inherited and aren't targeted by standard immunization vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h5)

question: Your patient has severe vomiting, dry lips and mouth, and poor skin turgor. What should you suspect?

options.A: Normal hydration levels
options.B: Acute kidney failure due to obstruction
options.C: Fluid volume excess
options.D: Fluid volume deficit

explanation: Dry mucous membranes and skin that takes a second to bounce back are classic textbook signs that the body has lost too much fluid (dehydration). [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h5)

question: A nurse washes her hands thoroughly with soap and water before entering a patient's room. Which group of germs is she mostly trying to wash away?

options.A: Resident microbiota
options.B: Systemic pathogens
options.C: Endogenous spores
options.D: Transient microbiota

explanation: Spot on! When you touch door handles or charts, you pick up temporary ('transient') microbes. Handwashing washes those casual hitchhikers right down the drain before you touch your patient. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the job of intrinsic activity when a drug acts in the body?

options.A: It measures the weight of the active pharmaceutical ingredient.
options.B: It prevents the drug from entering the bloodstream.
options.C: It triggers a biological response after the drug binds.
options.D: It determines how fast the kidneys clear the medicine.

explanation: Once the drug locks onto its receptor, intrinsic activity is the spark that actually makes the cell change its behavior. Great job learning the basics! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T5#GNS125_U5_T5_h2)

question: When working in emergency healthcare, what does the acronym MHPSS stand for?

options.A: Medical Health and Physical Social Services
options.B: Managed Hospital Patient Safety Systems
options.C: Multidisciplinary Healthcare Professional Support Staff
options.D: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support

explanation: You got this! MHPSS stands for Mental Health and Psychosocial Support. It covers both the emotional and social help people need during crises. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T5#GNS314_U6_T5_h1)

question: What does the term 'dual diagnosis' mean in psychiatric care?

options.A: A patient is evaluated by two different doctors on the same day
options.B: A patient has two different physical infections at the same time
options.C: A patient requires two different types of surgical operations
options.D: A patient has both a mental illness and a substance use disorder

explanation: Dual diagnosis describes individuals who experience a co-occurring psychiatric condition and substance use problem simultaneously. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care for a cancer patient receiving end-of-life support?

options.A: Testing new experimental medication regimens
options.B: Maximizing comfort and maintaining dignity
options.C: Restoring normal nutritional and metabolic status
options.D: Aggressively treating the underlying tumor growth

explanation: At the end of life, our nursing focus shifts completely to surrounding the patient and family with comfort, peace, and dignity. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h8)

question: Which cranial nerve carries taste messages from the front two-thirds of the tongue?

options.A: Trigeminal nerve (CN V)
options.B: Vagus nerve (CN X)
options.C: Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)
options.D: Facial nerve (CN VII)

explanation: The facial nerve handles taste for the front part of your tongue, sending those yummy signals straight to the brainstem. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T10#GNS211_U4_T10_h6)

question: What major part of a person's life is often shaken when a physical disability happens suddenly?

options.A: Their worldview and sense of identity
options.B: Their baseline laboratory blood values
options.C: Their physical height and bone density
options.D: Their cellular immune system response

explanation: A sudden disability turns a person's world upside down, changing how they see themselves and their future. Empathy goes a long way here! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T13#GNS225_U5_T13_h2)

question: How can a nurse manager use variable costs to plan staff schedules better?

options.A: By eliminating all fixed costs from the hospital accounting ledger
options.B: By anticipating supply needs and staffing levels based on patient admission trends
options.C: By ensuring that building rent decreases during slow hospital months
options.D: By stopping all purchases of direct patient care equipment

explanation: Knowing how costs and patient numbers move together helps you prepare enough hands on deck and supplies for busy seasons! [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why do the cells on the very outer layer of your skin not have nuclei?

options.A: They have been damaged by direct exposure to ultraviolet radiation
options.B: They are specialized immune cells that do not require genetic material
options.C: They are actively dividing stem cells that have temporarily discarded their DNA
options.D: They are dead, keratin-filled cells that have been pushed upward from deeper layers

explanation: Exactly right! As skin cells travel up from the bottom, they flatten, fill with tough keratin, lose their nuclei, and form a protective dead layer. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which chemical is most commonly used for high-level disinfection of heat-sensitive scopes?

options.A: Glutaraldehyde
options.B: Quaternary ammonium
options.C: Isopropyl alcohol
options.D: Sodium hypochlorite

explanation: You'll see glutaraldehyde often in clinical settings for delicate items like endoscopes that would melt or warp inside a hot autoclave. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why should a patient hold their breath for a few seconds after puffing their inhaler medication?

options.A: To allow the drug particles time to settle deep into the small airways
options.B: To prevent the medication from reaching the stomach and causing ulcers
options.C: To ensure that all excess carbon dioxide is pushed out of the blood
options.D: To force the heart rate to slow down after deep inspiration

explanation: Holding the breath gives gravity and time for those tiny medicine particles to land right where they are needed in the lungs, instead of just being breathed right back out! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T5#GNS223_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which cranial nerve is mainly responsible for controlling the muscles of the oesophagus?

options.A: Glossopharyngeal nerve
options.B: Hypoglossal nerve
options.C: Trigeminal nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

explanation: Correct! The vagus nerve is the major highway for signals that coordinate those smooth swallowing contractions. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h4)

question: What are the two main categories of hormone disorders?

options.A: Benign or malignant
options.B: Neural or humoral
options.C: Acute or chronic
options.D: Excess or deficiency

explanation: Keep it simple: hormone problems usually happen because the body makes either too much (excess) or too little (deficiency) of a hormone. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T6#GNS211_U1_T6_h8)

question: What is a mandatory safety action when a newborn is receiving phototherapy?

options.A: Keeping the incubator lights turned off at all times
options.B: Covering the infant's eyes with protective patches
options.C: Applying heavy moisturizing lotion to the skin every hour
options.D: Wrapping the baby tightly in warm blankets to prevent chills

explanation: Always make sure the baby's eyes are securely covered with eye patches to protect their delicate retina from the bright phototherapy lights. Safety first! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h9)

question: What is a major risk of overfeeding a critically ill patient on a ventilator?

options.A: Extra carbon dioxide production making it harder to breathe off the ventilator
options.B: Total elimination of the need for IV fluids
options.C: Rapid healing of surgical wounds
options.D: A sudden drop in blood sugar levels

explanation: Giving too many calories—especially from carbs—makes the body produce extra carbon dioxide. This makes breathing much harder for a patient trying to come off a ventilator! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h8)

question: What makes a saturated fatty acid different from an unsaturated fatty acid?

options.A: Saturated fats lack any hydrogen atoms along the carbon chain
options.B: Saturated fats contain only single carbon-to-carbon bonds
options.C: Saturated fats contain multiple carbon-to-carbon double bonds
options.D: Saturated fats always dissolve easily in plain water

explanation: Because they only have single bonds, saturated fat molecules pack tightly together, which is why they are usually solid at room temperature. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of performing a neurological examination?

options.A: To determine the exact blood type of the patient
options.B: To measure the patient's daily caloric intake
options.C: To diagnose specific psychiatric disorders
options.D: To evaluate the function of the nervous system

explanation: The neurological exam is specifically designed to assess how well the central and peripheral nervous systems are working. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of a unit dose cart on a hospital ward?

options.A: Serving as an emergency resuscitation trolley for cardiac arrest
options.B: Holding individual patient medication drawers for safe rounds
options.C: Transporting large bulk fluid bags from the main central store
options.D: Storing personal medical files and patient charts securely

explanation: The unit dose cart contains separate locked or labeled sections for each patient so the nurse can administer drugs safely bed-to-bed. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary reason nurses must master drug dosage calculations?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the hospital pharmacy
options.B: To speed up the hospital discharge process
options.C: To prevent medication errors and keep patients safe
options.D: To replace the need for physician order sheets

explanation: Accurate calculations ensure the patient receives the exact therapeutic amount, avoiding underdosing or dangerous toxicity. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is a major benefit of a man attending antenatal care visits with his partner?

options.A: He replaces the midwife during delivery
options.B: He can perform the physical examination himself
options.C: He learns about pregnancy danger signs and birth preparedness
options.D: He receives free medications for chronic illnesses

explanation: Attending antenatal visits helps fathers understand what complications to watch out for and how to prepare for emergencies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h3)

question: What is the usual recommended length of time to take nitrofurantoin for a simple bladder infection?

options.A: Twenty-one days
options.B: Fourteen days
options.C: A single dose
options.D: Five days

explanation: A short, sweet 5-day course is usually all it takes to clear a simple bladder infection while keeping side effects low. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h4)

question: When is a nurse most likely to use the rectal route of medication administration?

options.A: When the patient has severe vomiting and cannot swallow pills
options.B: When the patient prefers taking sweet liquids over tablets
options.C: When the drug is only available in a chewable tablet form
options.D: When the patient needs a slow-release oral multivitamin

explanation: Vomiting prevents oral medications from staying down, so the rectal route bypasses the upper gastrointestinal tract entirely. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h1)

question: You feel a patient's uterus (fundus) on her second day after birth and notice it feels soft and is higher than expected. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward
options.B: Massage the fundus gently until it becomes firm
options.C: Administer an intravenous fluid bolus
options.D: Document that the uterus is healing normally

explanation: A soft or 'boggy' uterus needs a little help! Massaging it gently makes the muscle fibers tighten up, which stops heavy bleeding. You're doing great. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h2)

question: A patient in a rural community gets taeniasis after eating locally prepared meat. What was the most likely cause?

options.A: Eating undercooked pork or beef containing live larval cysts
options.B: Drinking unboiled stream water contaminated with tapeworm segments
options.C: Sharing eating utensils with an infected family member
options.D: Working barefoot in muddy soil containing free-living larvae

explanation: Correct! You catch intestinal taeniasis strictly by eating raw or undercooked meat that has live cysts in it. Always ensure your meat is well cooked! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h3)

question: What is the most crucial piece of history to gather first when assessing an animal bite?

options.A: The exact weight and age of the bitted patient
options.B: The color and breed of the animal involved
options.C: The insurance and home address of the owner
options.D: The exact time of the bite and tetanus status

explanation: Timing tells us about infection risks, while checking the patient's tetanus status lets us know if a booster shot is urgently needed. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h3)

question: A pregnant woman misses her antenatal visits because she cannot afford transport or clinic fees. Which factor is mainly affecting her health?

options.A: Political party affiliation
options.B: Socio-economic factors
options.C: Cultural taboos
options.D: Genetic factors

explanation: Spot on! Financial struggles and poverty are classic examples of socio-economic factors that make it hard for patients to access care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h2)

question: What does 'cross-contamination' mean in a kitchen setting?

options.A: The transfer of harmful pathogens from one surface or food to another
options.B: The chemical reaction that occurs when mixing two different spices
options.C: The freezing of fresh vegetables at incorrect freezer temperatures
options.D: The natural spoilage of food caused by exposure to direct sunlight

explanation: Spot on! Cross-contamination happens when germs travel from a dirty source (like raw meat) over to safe food (like a fresh salad). [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h4)

question: A clinic team has ten great ideas but only enough time to test one. What should they do first?

options.A: Implement all ten ideas simultaneously to save time
options.B: Discard all ideas and keep the current routine unchanged
options.C: Use an impact-versus-effort matrix to filter and prioritize the ideas
options.D: Pick the longest and most expensive idea to look impressive

explanation: A prioritization matrix simply helps you weigh which idea will give the best results with a realistic amount of effort. Work smarter, not harder! [learn more](GST319_U3_T3#GST319_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following describes the difference between macronutrients and micronutrients?

options.A: Micronutrients are digested much faster than any macronutrient
options.B: Micronutrients are needed in smaller amounts and do not provide direct calories
options.C: Macronutrients are stored in bones while micronutrients float in blood
options.D: Macronutrients are only needed during childhood and growth phases

explanation: While macronutrients are consumed in large amounts for energy and structure, micronutrients are needed in tiny amounts to regulate body processes without supplying calories. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h3)

question: Why are strong people skills even more important in community nursing than in a big hospital?

options.A: Hospital nurses do not need to communicate with patients and families.
options.B: Patients in communities are more likely to reject care if they feel judged or misunderstood.
options.C: Community nurses rarely perform physical assessments or give medications.
options.D: Community settings have unlimited funding for medical technology.

explanation: Spot on! Since you are visiting people in their own private space, building a warm connection means everything. If they feel judged, they simply won't let you help. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical source of unwanted clinical variation?

options.A: Differences in individual clinician training and experience
options.B: Following strict, up-to-date evidence-based protocols
options.C: Inconsistent communication during nursing shift handovers
options.D: Varying availability of necessary medical supplies on wards

explanation: Exactly! Following solid, research-backed protocols actually reduces unwanted differences and helps us give better care. [learn more](GST319_U2_T4#GST319_U2_T4_h4)

question: A nurse manager sees that patient falls are increasing on the ward. What should they do first?

options.A: Suspend all nursing staff on duty immediately
options.B: Review incident reports and audit unit safety practices
options.C: Ignore the data because falls are common in hospitals
options.D: Give every patient a written academic test on mobility

explanation: Before jumping to conclusions, always look at the data and evaluate the root cause so you can fix the actual problem. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h7)

question: Which data quality rule means we should document care right after giving it?

options.A: Completeness
options.B: Consistency
options.C: Timeliness
options.D: Accessibility

explanation: Timeliness means writing things down promptly so the chart always reflects what is happening with the patient right now. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T7#GNS113_U2_T7_h2)

question: What does a negative correlation mean between two variables?

options.A: Both variables decrease at the exact same time.
options.B: There is no relationship whatsoever between the variables.
options.C: The data collected by the researcher is invalid.
options.D: As one variable increases, the other variable decreases.

explanation: You're doing great! Think of it like a seesaw: when one thing goes up (like daily exercise), the other thing goes down (like resting blood pressure). That is a negative correlation! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T8#GNS224_U1_T8_h3)

question: What do plant 'secondary metabolites' mainly do for the plant and for medicine?

options.A: Capturing sunlight exclusively for photosynthesis
options.B: Therapeutic and protective chemical effects
options.C: Storing plain water during heavy droughts
options.D: Providing basic structural cellulose for the stem

explanation: Plants make special chemicals like alkaloids to protect themselves from pests. Luckily for us, these exact same natural chemicals often have healing powers in humans! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T2#GNS125_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is it so important to talk to a suspected abuse survivor alone in a private room, away from family?

options.A: To ensure the patient feels safe to speak freely without fear of the abuser
options.B: To reduce the amount of paperwork the nursing staff must complete
options.C: To prevent other patients from hearing about medical equipment
options.D: To comply with hospital billing regulations for outpatient visits

question: How do daily community health records help with national health planning in Nigeria?

question: A mother who gave birth yesterday feels a sudden gush of blood every time she stands up. What is your best first step?

question: Clearing stagnant water around houses to reduce mosquito breeding sites is an intervention aimed at which part of the epidemiological triangle?

question: What are the three simple action steps in Psychological First Aid (PFA)?

question: If a diet study relies entirely on patients writing down what they ate in a diary, what limitation should you mention?

question: What is the primary goal of the living will movement?

question: Why do nurses view substance abuse as a chronic brain condition rather than a lack of willpower?

question: A nurse wants to study the shared daily habits and culture of nurses in a busy emergency room. Which research approach fits best?

question: An older adult started oxybutynin three days ago and is now suddenly confused and restless. What should you do?

explanation: Before jumping to conclusions, checking the background context helps you see if it's a new glitch or part of an old pattern. [learn more](GST319_U4_T5#GST319_U4_T5_h6)

question: When should a nurse apply standard precautions during patient care?

options.A: When working exclusively in surgical operating theaters
options.B: Only after a laboratory confirms a bloodborne pathogen
options.C: Only when caring for patients with confirmed viral infections
options.D: During the care of all patients regardless of their diagnosis

explanation: Standard precautions treat all body fluids as potentially infectious and must be used for every patient every time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h4)

question: You tell a nervous patient, 'I am not rushed at all,' but you keep checking your watch and eyeing the door. What will they believe?

options.A: The spoken words because nurses are always honest
options.B: That the clock is broken and the nurse is relaxed
options.C: The non-verbal cue that the nurse is in a rush
options.D: Both messages equally without any confusion

explanation: Spot on! When words and body language clash, patients almost always trust what your body is showing them. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h3)

question: How do modified utensils with built-in grips help a patient with failing fine motor control?

options.A: They compensate for weak grip strength and hand tremors
options.B: They completely cure the underlying nerve degeneration
options.C: They prevent the patient from feeling hungry
options.D: They make the food taste better and digest faster

explanation: Specialized grips provide better purchase for weak hands, allowing the patient to continue feeding themselves without assistance. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h5)

question: What is the most common cause of peripheral neuropathy worldwide?

options.A: Carpal tunnel syndrome
options.B: Diabetes mellitus
options.C: Guillain-Barré syndrome
options.D: Vitamin C deficiency

explanation: When blood sugar stays high over a long time, it slowly damages the tiny blood vessels that feed our nerves. That's why diabetes is the top cause of neuropathy! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h2)

question: Why is it smart for nurse managers to review staff feedback surveys about teamwork and collaboration?

options.A: To identify departmental friction points before they cause patient harm
options.B: To replace all human staff members with automated software
options.C: To decide which staff members deserve a pay cut
options.D: To eliminate the need for any future meetings

explanation: You got it! Surveys give the team a voice to point out where things are clashing, allowing managers to step in and fix things proactively. [learn more](GST321_U1_T12#GST321_U1_T12_h7)

question: Why do quantitative researchers try to remain completely neutral and detached from their study participants?

options.A: To avoid having to write detailed nursing care plans
options.B: To prevent personal bias from affecting the study results
options.C: To make it easier to recruit busy hospital staff
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of running the project

explanation: Staying objective ensures the data truly reflects reality, rather than what the researcher hopes or wishes to see. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T4#GNS224_U1_T4_h1)

question: How long should patients wait at the clinic after getting an immunization?

options.A: At least 15 minutes
options.B: Exactly two hours
options.C: Until the end of the market day
options.D: No waiting time is required

explanation: That 15-minute window is a crucial safety check just in case a rare allergic reaction pops up right away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h5)

question: What is the ultimate goal for many participants in a sheltered workshop?

options.A: Remaining in the workshop facility for their entire lives
options.B: Starting an independent manufacturing business alone
options.C: Becoming full-time nursing instructors in hospitals
options.D: Transitioning into open, competitive employment

explanation: These workshops are meant to be a helpful stepping stone toward regular, independent jobs in the community. Almost done with this set! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T7#GNS314_U5_T7_h7)

question: Why is knowing the route of transmission important for a nurse?

options.A: It eliminates the need for hand hygiene in clean wards
options.B: It predicts the exact day the patient will be discharged
options.C: It determines which antibiotic the doctor will prescribe first
options.D: It helps choose the correct isolation and barrier precautions

explanation: When nurses know how a germ travels, they can block that path using masks, gloves, or specific room placements. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h1)

question: Why is it so important to use a client-centered approach during family planning counseling?

options.A: It allows the nurse to choose the most expensive method available
options.B: It stops the client from asking questions about side effects
options.C: It guarantees that the client will choose permanent sterilization
options.D: It ensures the client selects a method that fits her lifestyle and health needs

explanation: Nursing is all about the patient! When a client helps choose her own method, she feels respected and is much more likely to use it correctly. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a legal duty of a nurse handling controlled drugs?

options.A: Changing the doctor's prescription order to match ward supplies
options.B: Reporting missing medication from the drug cupboard
options.C: Verifying the patient's identity before administration
options.D: Documenting every dose given accurately

explanation: Nurses cannot alter prescriptions; doing so is illegal and falsifies medical records. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h5)

question: What do we call it when an older adult takes several different medications at the same time?

options.A: Polydipsia
options.B: Hypertension
options.C: Hyperglycemia
options.D: Polypharmacy

explanation: Spot on! 'Poly' means many, and 'pharmacy' refers to drugs. Polypharmacy is super common in older adults who manage multiple health conditions. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T1#GNS324_U3_T1_h5)
